title: Working on Open Source Automatic 2D Character Rigging and Animation Pipeline
author: fyrean
selftext:
Last week,  [see-through](https://github.com/shitagaki-lab/see-through) came out. It is a robust model that can decompose a single static anime image into 23 different layers for rigging and animation. It greatly lowers the cost of entry for rigged animated 2D models! Unfortunately it is still extremely time consuming to manually process and rig the result PSD file with 23 different layers(30+ if you select split left right and by depth). A few years ago I looked into commissioning a custom Vtuber model and the cost for rigging the body parts alone is at least $500 and takes weeks, if not a few months! Its probably even more now with inflation... Sure you can learn to do it yourself, but live2d costs $100 a year, and Spine a whooping $379 (for pro version with actual mesh deform required for these kind of animations).

So my solution is not to create a live2d competitor, I am only a single person afterall. Hence I focused on a mesh-deform-capable program with the ability to automatically rig see-through models. It can account for different cases such as the legs or arms being merged together. You only need a few seconds to manually adjust where the joints should be (shoulders for arm movement, elbows, neck, head, ...). I also added DWPose which can automatically rig the entire model for you! But the download is a bit long at 50MB, and wont work on devices that don't have webGPU (tbh it would only take a little bit of time to adjust the joints yourself).

So the workflow is: static character image -> remove background -> [see-through](https://huggingface.co/spaces/24yearsold/see-through-demo) decomposition (free huggingface space)  -> my tool (stretchy studio) = automatic rigging and ready to animate instantly!

There are still alot of bugs I need to fix, hopefully I can release this soon. It is a React webapp that can manage different layers, with basic features like changing the draw order (like in live2d), the animation uses direct keyframing (like after effects) instead of live2d's parameter system. I am working on export options to more popular tools like Spine and Dragonbones. Sadly live2d is super closed source and doesnt have documentation on how to export their project.

I could release the source code right now but it would be quite messy.
